# Purpose

These answers are representative. Award credit for a centered axial load path, correct rectangular areas, identification of the minimum-area section, consistent N-mm-MPa units, and summation of all segment elongations.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The base problem uses average axial stress and prismatic-segment elongation. Local fillet stress concentration, pin-hole net-section stress, bearing, connection strength, fatigue, fracture, residual stress, and out-of-plane effects require additional geometry and material data.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

Suggested weighting:

- context interpretation and load path: 15%;
- idealization and assumptions: 15%;
- critical section and allowable load: 30%;
- segment and total elongation: 30%;
- engineering recommendation and limitations: 10%.
